acceptance: Document an opt-in shared coordinator and stable project identity while preserving the default offline/local workflow.
Two independent clones claiming overlapping scope have exactly one winner under the selected coordination mode.
Test expiry, fencing, partitions, recovery and explicit offline behavior; never imply global ownership from local ASSIGNED state.
Keep shared data minimal and preserve zero additional capture model calls; disclose network requirements for the optional mode.
payload.description:
Scope boundary. QA baseline: DIP v0.3.2, 6 October 2026.

Live claims are local to a shared Git worktree family. Independent clones and computers merge durable intent through Git but do not share live leases. Push/merge alone cannot prevent simultaneous execution or guarantee exclusivity.

Evidence and starting points: docs/compatibility.md, docs/automation.md, README.md.

This is unassigned contributor backlog, not implemented work. Preserve the existing license, DCO and local/offline defaults.
payload.title: DIP-L05: Design opt-in coordination across independent clones and machines
